ὑποδέρω.definition: strip off the skin a little or below, Gal.2.700, 18.103, Orib.46.15.5

ὑποδέχομαι.definition: in Ion. and Dor. Prose Hdt. (v; entertain to a meal, Antipho1.18, cf. IG4.679.15 ; Th.6.22; the host , Epict.Fr.17; D.S.17.115, cf. Plu.Alex.23

ὑποδορά.definition: gradual stripping of the skin, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.15.5, Antyll.ib.45.25.5, Aët.15.8

ὑποζεύγνυμι.definition: pf. Orus ap.EM786.5:—yoke under; metaph., subjugate, Orus l. c.:—Pass., submit to, S.Aj.24

ὑποζέω.definition: ferment a little, begin to ferment, Gp.6.12.2

ὑποθερμαίνω.definition: heat a little, Gal.11.417:—Pass., grow somewhat hot, Il.16.333, 20.476, cf. Hp.Ulc.26: metaph., Luc.DMeretr.8.3

ὑποθέω.definition: fut. make a secret attack; cut in before, in running a race, supplant, Ar.Eq.1161; of a solar eclipse, . . Cleom.2.3; Them.Or.26.317b

ὑποθήγω.definition: whet, Ael.NA5.45; sharpen, make acute, ib.9.16; stimulate, ib.5.39: metaph., provoke him to rise, ib.8.2:—Pass., Id.Fr.81

ὑποθωρήσσομαι.definition: Med., arm oneself in secret, Il.18.513

ὑποϊάχω.definition: sound forth a little or in answer, AP9.314

ὕποινος.definition: under the influence of wine; full of wine, Philostr.Im.1.31; ib.18

ὑποκαίω.definition: Att. burn by applying fire below; light under, Luc.Phal.1.11:—Pass., Arist.Mete.355a17

ὑποκάμπτω.definition: bend short back, they; intr., turn back, double as a hare, X.Cyn.5.16

ὑποκάτω.definition: Adv. below, under, c. gen; in Logic, the subordinate genus, opp. Arist.Top.143a21; ib.122a9, al

ὑποκλίνω.definition: bend under or in subjection to; give way to, Herm.in Phdr.p.157 A.: so intr. in Act., . . Orph.A.848

ὑποκλονέομαι.definition: Pass., to be driven in confusion before; to be shaken so as to fall, Q.S.14.572

ὑποκλοπέομαι.definition: Pass., lurk in secret places, Od.22.382

ὑποκρύπτω.definition: hide under or beneath, [the ship] was hidden beneath the spray, Il.15.626:—Med., keep something secret from him, v.l. in X.An.1.9.19, cf. J.BJ1.31.4:— Pass., Sor.2.64

ὑποκρώζω.definition: croak faintly, as a sick person, Luc.D Mort.6.4

ὑποκύπτω.definition: stoop under a yoke; c. acc., stoop it so as to let a load be put on, Ar.Ach.954

ὑπολέγω.definition: dictate, prompt, Plu.2.46b; consider, take into account, . . D.C.54.15

ὑπολείβω.definition: pour libations, A.Ag.69 :—Pass., percolate, trickle down, Hp.Mul.1.34, Nic.Al.24

ὑπολείπω.definition: also , leave remaining; of things, fail one, Lys.27.1 , cf. Arr.Ind.26.9 ; Gorg.17; Arist.Rh.1374a33; Id.Pol.1330b7

ὑπολευκαίνομαι.definition: Pass., become white underneath or somewhat white, Il.5.502, cf. Arat.927, Luc.DMeretr.11.3, etc

ὑπολοπάω.definition: peel, lose the bark, cj. Schneid. in Thphr.HP5.1.4

ὑπολύω.definition: loosen beneath or below, made; loose from under the yoke, Il.23.513, cf. Od.4.39; Th.4.128; loose from under the sheep, Od.9.463:—Med., . . thou didst set him free from bonds, Il.1.401

ὑπόμισθος.definition: serving for pay, hired, of persons; farmed out, Id.Alex.49

ὑπομοσχεύω.definition: ) propagate by layers: metaph., propagate, Eun.Hist.p.271 D

ὑπομύω.definition: only pf. part., half-closed eyes, Alciphr.3.55

ὑπονεάω.definition: break up fallow ground with the plough, Thphr.HP3.1.6

ὑπονίζω.definition: wash slightly or beneath, Hierocl.p.58 A

ὑποξέω.definition: scrape underneath, Hippiatr.104; wipe underneath, ib.11

ὑποπάλλω.definition: rebound, 'repeat', of swallowed food, Ruf; Pass., throb a little, Agath.4.25

ὑποπέμπω.definition: send under, to, or into, c. acc; send as a spy, send in a false character, X.An.2.4.22, cf. Th. l.c., and v. foreg

ὑποπερκάζω.definition: begin to assume a dark colour, begin to turn, of grapes, Od.7.126, cf. Ph.2.54:—Med., Ach.Tat.2.3; cf

ὑποπίπτω.definition: fut. Phld.Mort.32:—fall under or; fall down, cringe before any one, Pl.R.576a, X.Cyn.10.18: hence, to be subject to him, fall under his power, Isoc.7.12: also of a flatterer, cringe to, fawn on, Is.6.29, D.45.63, 65,5…

ὑποπλέω.definition: sail under, i.e. under the lee of; sail underground, D.C.49.43

ὑποπνέω.definition: blow underneath, Arist.Pr.887b30: used for; blow gently, Act.Ap.27.13

ὑποπτάω.definition: roast a little, dub. for Thphr.HP4.8.14

ὕπορθος.definition: more or less upright, propped up in bed; perh. almost direct to

ὑπορρέω.definition: flow under or beneath, Arist.Mir.843a21; infiltrate, Hp.Loc.Hom.29

ὑπορρήγνυμι.definition: in Pass., the air is cleft beneath from heaven on high, Il.8.558, 16.300

ὑποσαίρω.definition: grin a little, show one's teeth a; burst, of over-ripe fruit, Philostr.Im.1.31

ὑποσακίζω.definition: strain or filter away; trot, go briskly forward, Ael.Dion.Fr.296

ὑποσείω.definition: Ep. rotate, spin round; hold out or throw to, Ael.NA7.13

ὑποστάζω.definition: intr., drop slowly, Gloss.; to have a running at the nose, v.l. in Hp.Coac.205

ὑποσταχύομαι.definition: Pass., yield increase like ears of corn: metaph., Od.20.212.—Later we find an Act., as v.l. in A.R.1.972

ὑποστίζω.definition: make somewhat variegated or spotted; Gramm., put a comma, Phlp.in Mete.99.10

ὑποστρέφω.definition: turn round about or back, Il.5.581; roll up, Arist.Pr.895b10

ὑποτάκτης.definition: one who brings into subjection, : PMag. Leid.V.7.11

ὑποταρβέω.definition: to be somewhat afraid of, shrink before, Il.17.533

ὑποτελής.definition: subject to taxes, tributary; Act., receiving payment, c. gen., Luc.Merc.Cond.36

ὑποτίθημι.definition: place under a certain class, etc., Pl.Plt.289a; subjoin, enclose, append a document, PLille4.2 , cf. Sammelb.5675.2 , etc.: so in Med., PLond.3.921.10

ὑποτιμάω.definition: name the price of what one offers for sale; make a return or assessment of one's property, Arist.Oec.1347a22, 1353a12

ὑποτρέχω.definition: aor. : poet. pf; run under, stretch away under, h.Ap.284

ὑποτρέω.definition: Ep. 3pl. pres. Timo58.4: Hom. only in aor. back, give ground, Il.7.217, 15.636, 17.275; Pi.Fr.224: c. acc., shrink before, flee before, Il.17.587. Poet. word, used in late Prose, Plu.Mar.7, M.Ant.11.9

ὑποτρομέω.definition: = tremble under; c. acc., tremble before any one, . . 20.28: without acc., 22.241

ὑποτροφή.definition: supply of nourishment, sustenance; growth, Max. Tyr.29.1

ὑποτυπόω.definition: sketch out, outline, Arist.EN1098a21; predispose, Phld.Mus.p.57 K., cf. p.77 K

ὑποφέρω.definition: fut. S.El.834 , Phld.Lib.p.28 O; bring close together, Id.HA604b1

ὑποφεύγω.definition: Ion. Iterat. v.l. in; abs., retire a little, withdraw, Hdt.4.111,120, Th.3.97; evade, Pl.Lg.762b

ὑποφθάνω.definition: aor. A.R.4.307; part; c. acc., to be beforehand with one, A.R. l.c., Plu.Aem.26, etc.:—Med., Od.15.171, cf. AP9.227

ὑπόφθονος.definition: somewhat jealous, only in Adv., behave somewhat jealously towards one, Id.HG7.1.26

ὑποφορά.definition: carrying off below, purging; draining off, Sor.1.58

ὑποφυράω.definition: throw into confusion, to have done some cooking of the accounts, Cic.Att.6.5.1

ὑποφύω.definition: cause to grow up under; Pass., of muscles, to be inserted under, Gal.2.246, UP3.11, cf. 4.10, al

ὑποχαλάω.definition: slacken a little, lower; intr. = Pass., Anon.Prog.inRh.1.621 W

ὑπόχαλκος.definition: containing a mixture of copper; sounding like copper, Philostr.VA3.8

ὑποχαυνόω.definition: make somewhat conceited, puff up, Plu.2.21c; letting his words die away half-finished , Procop.Gaz.p.159B

ὑποχέω.definition: aor. Ep. only form of the; in Hom. only of dry things, strew or spread under, Il.11.843, Od.14.49, cf. 16.47:—Pass., the leaves fallen and scattered under the feet, Hdt.7.218

ὑποψάλλω.definition: touch softly, prop. of the strings of the lyre: metaph., invites them to sing, Philostr.VA7.11

ὑπόψιος.definition: under the eye or view, conspicuous, Opp.H.1.30

ὑποψοφέω.definition: make a slight noise; snapping her fingers in accompaniment, Plu.2.336c

ὑποψωνέω.definition: underbid in the purchase of victuals or buy up underhand, Ar.Ach.842

ὑπτιάζω.definition: lay oneself back, fall back; metaph., of haughty persons, carry oneself with languid arrogance, Aeschin.1.132

ὑπτιάω.definition: only in Ep. part. and 3sg. subj. poet. for intr., of the moon's crescent, lean backward, Arat.789,795

ὑπτιότης.definition: supine position, of leaves; of a river, flatness, Str.8.3.19

ὑπτιόω.definition: only in Pass., to be turned on one's back; of land, slope gently upwards, . . J.AJ15.11.3

ὑπωθέω.definition: push or thrust away; push up from beneath, Hp.Art.7

ὑπωμία.definition: Ion. the part under the shoulders, Hp. ap.Gal.19.150

ὑπώρειος.definition: under the mountains, Callistr.Stat.1: but ib.14

ὕφαλμος.definition: somewhat salt, Dsc.3.136 ; also ibid. as f.l. for

ὕφαλος.definition: under the sea, the; metaph., secret, crafty, of men, EM785.44; Gal.19.489

ὑφέλκω.definition: draw away under, draw away underhand or gently, draw one away by the two feet, Il.14.477; draw away by undermining, Th.2.76, cf. D.C.66.4; Plu.2.781e; i.e. to be slippery, Poll.1.187: —Med., I trail Persian slippers u…

ὑφέρπω.definition: creep on secretly; c. acc., Philostr.VA1.37; secretly aim at, Hld.10.19

ὑφιδρύω.definition: subordinate, place under control of . . , Plot.6.9.3

ὑφίημι.definition: Ion. Hdt.1.156, al.:—let down, lower; put under, Il.14.240, cf. Od.19.57; X.Cyn.10.2; put a young one under its dam, put it to suck, Od.9.245,309; Theoc.4.4:—but in Med., put it to her own breasts, to suckle it, E.Ph.31

ὑφίστημι.definition: Ion. Hdt.5.16, al.: fut; post secretly or in ambush, X.HG4.1.26

ὑφορμάω.definition: to be in motion under, metaph., Adam.Vent.36 :—Pass., aor. part. darting back, read by Ar.Byz. for in Il.16.313

ὑφορμέω.definition: lie at anchor in wait for others, Plb.3.19.8; lit., anchor under, D.Chr.11.116, cf. 7.2

ὕφορμος.definition: anchorage, Arist.HA542b23; Adj., fit for anchoring in, Id.14.1.35; St.Byz. s.v

ὑψηχής.definition: making a loud or ringing sound, because of their loud neighing, or their 'high-resounding pace' , Il.5.772 , 23.27; Philostr.VS1.25.7

ὑψιβίας.definition: Boeot. or high and mighty, Corinn.13

ὑψίνομος.definition: feeding on high places, of the goat, Eust.472.11

ὑψιπαγής.definition: high-built, towering; set on high, Nonn.D.2.712

ὑψίπους.definition: gen. high-footed, i.e. high- reared, lofty, S.OT866

ὑψίπρῳρος.definition: with high prow, ibid. ; Orac. ap. Porph. ap. Eus.PE5.9

ὑψιτενέω.definition: aim high, Theoctist. ap. Stob. vol. vp.1146 Hense

ὕψωμα.definition: elevation, height; Astrol., exaltation of a heavenly body, opp. Plu.2.149a, 782d, S.E.M.5.33, Ptol.Tetr.37

ὕψωσις.definition: hill, eminence, Str.7.5.10; metaph., exalting, glorifying, LXXPs.149.6

υἷς.definition: Adv. as far as, SIG1 : cf

ὕπαιθα.definition: Adv., out under, under and away; Prep. with gen. under, under him, so as to support him, Il.18.421; of one shrinking under an attack, 21.255

ὕπαντα.definition: Adv., c. dat., intervening in . . , cj. Hartung in E.Supp.398

ὑπέκ.definition: before a vowel poet. Prep. with gen., out from under, from beneath, away from, etc., Il.13.89, 15.628, al.; A.R.4.933, cf. Q.S.4.402

ὑπέρ.definition: Ep. also used by Hom. only in the phrase ; Arc. : in Aeol. replaced by : Prep. governing gen. and acc., in Arc. also dat. A. WITH GENIT., I. of Place, over; 1. in a state of rest, over, above, freq. in Hom., . . Il.4.…

ὑπόδρα.definition: Ep. Adv., used only in the phrase looking from under the brows, looking askance, grimly, Il.1.148, al.; cf

ὑποδράξ.definition: Adv., later form for Call.Fr.anon.63, Nic.Th.457,765

ὑποκλαδόν.definition: Adv. with the knees somewhat bent, inclined a little or gradually, Opp.C.4.205

ὑποπρό.definition: or Prep. c. gen. just before; Thess. of Time, before, the former decree [i.e. that of four years earlier] and the present one, IG9.517.43 , cf. 512.30 : with perh. supply but the sense of the whole phrase is simply th…

ὑποφθαδόν.definition: Adv. striving to be first, in rivalry; taking one unawares, ib.5.387

ὕψι.definition: Adv. on high, aloft, Il.13.140; ib.371; 20.155, cf. Od.16.264; . . . . Hes.Op.204; . . from high on the ships, Il.15.387; . . 16.374; . . out at sea, 14.77

ὑψόθεν.definition: Boeot. prob. in Corinn.Supp.1.32, Adv; = aloft, on high, A.Supp.381 ; opp. AP12.97

ὕψοι.definition: Adv. upwards, v.l. for in Sapph.91

ὑψοῦ.definition: metaph., having praised me highly, Hdt.9.79; S.OT914. cf
